To find the stationary points of an equation y = f(x), first find the first derivative of the function (f'(x)). Then, set the first derivative equal to zero and solve for x. The solutions are the x-coordinates of the stationary points. Next, find the second derivative of the function (f''(x)). Finally, evaluate the second derivative at each stationary point. If f''(x) > 0, the point is a local minimum. If f''(x) < 0, the point is a local maximum. If f''(x) = 0, the test is inconclusive.
